steps.body: Trading works because ten of one unit and one of the next are the same amount: 14 tens IS 1 hundred and 4 tens.
steps.narration: Trading works because ten of one unit and one of the next are the same amount: 14 tens IS 1 hundred and 4 tens.

widget.prompt: Build 343 as 2 flats, 14 rods, 3 cubes — a legal non-standard form.

commonBuilds.feedback: 2 flats, 4 rods, 3 cubes make only 243 — the ten extra rods are part of the number.

widget.missFeedback: That build names a different number — total each unit's worth and match 343 exactly.
widget.successFeedback: 2 hundreds, 14 tens, 3 ones — exactly 343 wearing its traded-down outfit.

predict.prompt: 2 hundreds, 14 tens, 3 ones: is that a real number?
predict.reveal: Fourteen tens are 140; with 200 and 3 that is 343. Standard form is a convention, not a law.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2b why trade.
invariants: Trading between places changes the FORM of a quantity, never its value — the model and the number must stay equal for g2b why trade.
misconceptions: Treating a trade as adding or removing amount instead of renaming the same total.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the blocks stop matching the written number?

widget.prompt: 1 hundreds, 16 tens, and 1 ones make what number?

commonErrors.feedback: The ten tens you can bundle into a hundred vanished instead of trading up.
That treated every ten as a hundred; only groups of TEN tens trade up.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the places up — hundreds with hundreds, tens with tens, ones with ones — and work one column at a time.

widget.prompt: A build shows 12 tens. What does trading do with them?

options.label: Trade ten of the tens for one hundred
options.feedback: Correct — ten tens and one hundred are the same amount, so trading changes the form, never the value.

options.label: Throw away the extra tens
options.feedback: Discarding tens shrinks the number; a trade must keep the total exactly equal.

options.label: Turn each ten into a hundred
options.feedback: One ten is worth ten, not a hundred; only a GROUP of ten tens equals one hundred.

options.label: Leave 12 tens — numbers cannot hold that many
options.feedback: A number can hold 12 tens perfectly well; standard form just prefers the traded version.
